correctness.rationale: For all even \(m=2q\ge6\), \(\var\(\varepsilon\)ilon\in(0,2/15)\), positive Fourier coefficients imply strict RKHS PD, analytic kernel, and a unique top-three eigenspace. Distinct node sets both have \(\Phi^*\Phi=mI_3\) by q-gon sums for orders 1,2. At the regular grid, the explicit orthonormal vector \((\psi_0-\psi_m-\psi_{-m})/\sqrt3\) lies perpendicular to every translate, so \(F\ge1/3\). At the staggered grid a displayed finite kernel combination matches each top target and cancels both high spikes; remaining RKHS squared norm is \(\le\var\(\varepsilon\)ilon(1-2^{1-m})/\lambda_t\), summing to \((5/2)\var\(\varepsilon\)ilon(1-2^{1-m})\). \(F(S)>0\) by the Vandermonde argument. This proves the strict inequality and unbounded factor, independently of the 16 numerical tests in verify.py.

value.rationale: Spectral landmark selection is a motivated numerical approximation objective whose relation to equal spacing and tight leading-mode frames is nontrivial when \(m>s\). The theorem isolates a real aliasing obstruction: both sets have *identical optimal* leading-eigenfunction conditioning while their full-RKHS projector losses differ by a factor unbounded in \(\varepsilon\). The result is uniform in all even landmark counts, uses an analytic strictly PD kernel with a top-three spectral gap, supplies an explicit geometric de-aliasing design, and cautions against optimizing only tight-frame surrogates. Although a constructed nonmonotone spectrum rather than a Gaussian family, the separation is mathematically substantive and reproducible.
